summary: Android capture plans now pass profile dimensions and frame-rate limits to MediaProjection. The virtual display is capped by its longest edge while preserving full-display orientation and app-only content aspect ratio. A rate gate limits frames forwarded to the WebRTC video source. The existing permission, foreground-service and OS-stop lifecycle remains in place. iOS is explicitly left without capture-time profile support claims.

checks.name: Screen capture dimension and frame-rate helper unit tests
checks.observation: 12 pure Java tests passed for nested profile-constraint parsing, orientation, aspect-preserving size caps, odd dimensions, rate limiting and capture-generation reset. This does not compile or exercise Android MediaProjection APIs.

checks.name: Flutter tests and analyzer
checks.observation: The repository-native check stopped before running tests because the Flutter executable is unavailable in PATH.

checks.name: Android plugin compile and app build
checks.observation: The Flutter app has no gradlew.bat script and Gradle is unavailable in PATH; pure helper JUnit tests are not a substitute for the Android build.

checks.name: Physical Android and iOS capture acceptance
checks.observation: No device capture was performed. Cadence, app-only/full-display selection, orientation, background transitions, permissions, interruption, OS stop, receiver frames, FPS, thermal behavior and iOS runtime support remain unverified.

limitations: The Android rate gate drops frames before they reach the WebRTC video source but does not reduce MediaProjection compositor cadence; power and thermal effects need device measurements.
The active profile is a maximum edge request. Actual output can be smaller than the selected profile and must be read from runtime counters.
iOS keeps its current ReplayKit path and legacy capture request. The new Android profile controls are not claimed for iOS.
remaining: Run the repository Flutter tests, analyzer and Android app build in CI. On physical Android, execute low-to-high-to-low, portrait/landscape, app-only resize and full-display, OS stop and user-initiated restart, background/resume with microphone on/off, permission denial and interruption scenarios with a remote viewer. Record capture/encoded/decoded counters, actual cadence, frame age, CPU and available thermal signals. Separately document iOS ReplayKit publication/receiver support and fallback behavior. Keep issue gates open until required runtime acceptance passes.
